keywords.great bath: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro is a masterpiece of hydraulic engineering, lined with bitumen and fine baked bricks to prevent water seepage.
keywords.bath: The Great Bath was used for sacred ritual purification and collective bathing during special seasonal ceremonies.
keywords.granary: The Great Granary at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro stored massive food reserves with air ducts to keep grain dry.
keywords.drainage: Harappan towns featured the world's first underground covered brick drainage systems with inspection manholes.
keywords.drain: Underground drains ran along wide grid streets, disposing wastewater safely outside the city citadel.
keywords.seal: Steatite seals featuring the Unicorn, Pashupati, and bull motifs were used by traders for official cargo stamping.
keywords.steatite: Soft steatite stone was carved and baked to craft intricate seals depicting sacred animals and Harappan script.
keywords.script: The Indus script remains an un-deciphered logo-syllabic writing system written right-to-left on stone seals.
keywords.mohenjo: Mohenjo-daro means 'Mound of the Dead' in Sindhi and was one of the largest planned cities of the ancient world.
keywords.harappa: Harappa was a major fortified urban hub known for modern brick size standards (1:2:4 ratio) and organized municipal planning.
keywords.dholavira: Dholavira in Gujarat is famous for its 16 colossal sandstone water reservoirs and massive stone signage.
keywords.lothal: Lothal had the world's earliest known tidal dockyard connecting Harappan merchants to ancient Mesopotamia.

general_lore: Pranam, mere aaka! The Harappan masters created grid-planned cities, subterranean drainage, and stone seals over 4,500 years ago!
